source: Kandal Provincial Department of Agriculture (មន្ទីរកសិកម្មខេត្តកណ្តាល), "ដំណំពោត" (Corn Crop / Zea mays production manual), 2015
text:
Aphids (ថេ, Aphid): several aphid species affect corn.

Melon aphid (Melon Aphid): this aphid is yellowish and lacks wings when it is on the crop. It is commonly found underneath the leaves and can build up to populations of around 1,500 per square meter under favorable conditions. Melon aphid does not usually feed heavily enough on corn itself to cause direct feeding damage of the same severity as on cucurbit crops, but it excretes honeydew, which promotes sooty mold growth on leaves, and importantly it can carry and transmit plant viruses such as Cucumber mosaic virus, succinct-yellow virus, and watermelon mosaic virus to related crops.

Corn leaf aphid (Rhopalosiphum maidis): this aphid is shaped similarly to other aphids, with a body about 1-2 mm long and around 6 legs. It commonly colonizes the whorl of the tassel and forms dense colonies on the corn plant's tassel and upper leaves, causing honeydew buildup and consequent sooty mold, which reduces the plant's photosynthetic capacity.

Biological control (natural enemies): natural predators that help control aphid populations include lady beetles (Hippodamia), lacewings, syrphid fly larvae, and parasitic wasps such as Lysiphlebus, Aphidius, Diaeretiella, and the group Aphelinus, which can help suppress melon aphid and related aphid populations.

Cultural and chemical control measures: remove and burn plant debris and weeds around the field edge that can harbor aphids; use resistant varieties where available; where chemical control is needed, apply insecticide only when infestation is severe, taking care that pesticide use does not also kill the natural enemy populations that would otherwise limit aphid numbers.
